lineItems.name: SDG&E delivery – time-of-use electricity
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for SDG&E to maintain the power lines and deliver electricity to your home.

lineItems.name: SDCP generation – electricity supply
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the actual electricity you used, provided by San Diego Community Power.

lineItems.name: Power Charge Indifference Adjustment (PCIA)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This fee covers costs for older power contracts SDG&E signed before you switched to a community provider.

lineItems.name: Base Services Charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a fixed monthly fee that helps cover the cost of your meter and basic grid infrastructure.

lineItems.name: Wildfire Fund charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state-mandated fee used to help fund wildfire safety and liability costs.

lineItems.name: Local taxes and other adjustments
lineItems.plainEnglish: These are standard local taxes and fees required by your city or county.

analysis.summary: Your bill is driven by your total usage of 612 kWh, with about 40% of that energy consumed during the expensive 4-9 PM on-peak window. You are currently served by SDCP for generation, which is reflected in your charges.
analysis.topSavingTip: Since 40% of your energy was used during the 4-9 PM peak window, try shifting heavy appliance use like laundry or dishwashing to before 4 PM or after 9 PM to lower your bill.

lineItems.name: Gas Service
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the natural gas you used during this billing period.

lineItems.name: Gas Energy Charge (31 of 32 Days)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This covers the cost of the gas supply for the majority of your billing cycle.

lineItems.name: Gas Energy Charge (1 of 32 Days)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This covers the cost of the gas supply for the final day of your billing cycle due to a rate change.

lineItems.name: California Climate Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state-mandated credit to help lower your energy costs.

lineItems.name: Public Purpose Program
lineItems.plainEnglish: This fee funds public programs like energy efficiency and low-income assistance.

lineItems.name: State Regulatory Fee
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a small fee to cover the state's costs for regulating utility services.

lineItems.name: Electricity Delivery (31 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost to transport electricity to your home over SDG&E's power lines.

lineItems.name: Electricity Delivery (1 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the delivery cost for the final day of your billing cycle.

lineItems.name: DWR Bond Charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state charge to pay off bonds issued during the 2001 energy crisis.

lineItems.name: Electricity Generation (31 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the actual electricity you consumed during the first 31 days.

lineItems.name: Electricity Generation (1 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the electricity you consumed on the final day of the billing cycle.

lineItems.name: DWR Revenue Adjustment
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a small adjustment related to state power contracts.

lineItems.name: Baseline Adjustment Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a discount for staying within your baseline energy allowance.

lineItems.name: California Climate Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state-mandated credit to help lower your electric energy costs.

analysis.summary: Your bill reflects usage of 757 kWh of electricity and 45 therms of gas. About 24% of your total electricity usage occurred during the expensive 4-9 PM on-peak window.
analysis.topSavingTip: Since you are on a Time-of-Use plan, try shifting energy-intensive chores like laundry or dishwashing to the super off-peak hours to avoid the higher on-peak rates.
